AI Overview
To change a ceramic product photo to a three-quarter view while preserving its shape and material, you can use 3D modeling, generative AI editing tools, or traditional product reshooting. Because ceramics have unique glazes, reflections, and textures, keeping them perfectly consistent when rotating an object in a 2D image can be challenging.
Here are the most effective methods to achieve this:
1. Generative AI Tools (Fastest & Easiest)
Modern AI tools allow you to manipulate existing objects or generate new angles using text prompts and image references.
AI Product Photography Platforms: Tools like Flair.ai, Mokker.ai, or Pebblely specialize in product photos. You can upload your original image as a reference and use their positioning tools or text prompts (e.g., "a three-quarter view of the ceramic vase") to generate the new angle.
Adobe Photoshop (Generative Fill): You can use Photoshop's 3D utilities or select the object and use Generative Fill to describe the angle you want. However, it may require a few generations to get the material texture and shape completely accurate.
2. 3D Modeling and Rendering (Most Precise)
If you need mathematical precision where the shape and material reflection look exactly the same across multiple marketing assets, 3D modeling is the industry standard.
Photogrammetry: You can use a smartphone app (like Polycam or RealityScan) to take multiple photos of your ceramic piece from different angles. The app stitches these photos into a highly accurate 3D model that retains the exact shape and texture. You can then open this model in free software like Blender and rotate the camera to a perfect three-quarter view.
3D Replicating: A 3D artist can recreate your ceramic item in software like Blender or Rhino, matching the exact dimensions. They will apply a custom digital material (shader) that mimics your ceramic glaze (matte, glossy, or crackle) and render it from a three-quarter angle.
3. Workflow Comparison
Method	Accuracy of Material/Shape	Speed	Cost
Generative AI	Medium (May warp subtle details)	Very Fast (Minutes)	Low / Free
Photogrammetry (3D Scan)	High (Captures real-world texture)	Medium (Hours)	Low (App based)
Manual 3D Modeling	Perfect (Fully customizable)	Slow (Days)	Medium to High
